# Toppförvaltaren: Därför investerar jag i storbanker och lastvagnar

**Feed**: dagen-med-di  
**Published**: 2026-10-14  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

A fund manager running the Swedish Value Fund, a top-performing actively managed Sweden fund (+17% so far this year), sees plenty of risks: rising long-term interest rates, government budget deficits in the US and France, worries about overspending on AI, and Ukraine. He is still optimistic over the long run and does not expect excessive pessimism in the short run, citing positive PMI readings and upbeat comments from the companies he talks to. He is clearly overweight the big Nordic banks, arguing they deserve a structural re-rating to P/E around 15, and the heavy-truck makers Volvo and Traton, which keep double-digit margins and have service moats against Chinese rivals. Ericsson is a recent value addition he holds ahead of its report.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 SWED-A — Swedbank | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Top holding in a fund with a clear bank overweight; the guest sees more upside and a P/E re-rating toward 15.

#### Reasoning

Guest (fund manager) holds the banks overweight. Higher rates, PMI, budding consumer optimism and corporate investment are driving credit demand. Balance sheets are strong, lending is stricter and credit losses over the cycle have been negligible, so banks behave like predictable cash-flow machines. He agrees with Sundling on a structural re-rating from P/E 12-13 toward 15. He sees the bank tax as already priced in.

#### Sell Triggers

- if credit growth stalls
- if a bank tax beyond current expectations is introduced
- if credit losses rise materially

> *"Vi tycker att vi har fått bra betalt, men att det finns mer att hämta."*

---

### 🟢 NDA-SE — Nordea | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Top holding; the guest's bank re-rating thesis applies.

#### Reasoning

Same thesis as the other banks: the guest overweights the big banks on risk-adjusted upside, supportive rates and credit demand, strong capital and low credit risk. The Nordic fiscal position lowers the need for punitive bank taxes compared with the rest of Europe. Re-rating toward P/E 15 is plausible.

#### Sell Triggers

- if credit demand weakens
- if a punitive bank tax is introduced
- if rates fall sharply

> *"Så i det fallet är jag benägen att hålla med Mattias."*

---

### 🟢 SEB-A — SEB | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Top holding in the overweight bank position; the guest sees more upside.

#### Reasoning

The guest's banks-as-cash-flow-machines thesis: strong balance sheets, stringent lending, negligible losses over the cycle and rising credit demand. He sees room for a structural P/E re-rating from 12-13 toward 15, as in the US.

#### Sell Triggers

- if credit growth stalls
- if the bank tax is harsher than communicated
- if credit losses rise

> *"Men vi har fortsatt att ha en klar övervikt i ett antal banker där vi har sett att den riskjusterade potentialen har varit god."*

---

### 🟡 SHB-A — Handelsbanken | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Still held but trimmed because credit growth has lagged its peers.

#### Reasoning

The guest still owns Handelsbanken and the sector thesis applies, but he reduced the position because its credit growth has not kept pace with peers. It sits below the other big banks in his preference.

#### Sell Triggers

- if credit growth keeps lagging peers

> *"Handelsbanken har också utvecklats hyfsat, men deras kredittillväxt har inte riktigt hängt med. Det har gjort att vi har hyvlat lite där."*

---

### 🟢 VOLV-B — Volvo | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Top holding: double-digit margins even at low volumes, very strong balance sheet, still cheap.

#### Reasoning

The guest argues the trucks business has structurally changed and now stays profitable with double-digit margins in downturns, with a very strong balance sheet. He thinks the market's memory has not caught up, so the valuation is too low. On the weaker ACT orders, he notes this year's capacity is sold out and the 2027 order books have just opened. On China, he sees service and aftermarket as a significant moat.

#### Sell Triggers

- if margins fall below double digits in a downturn
- if Chinese competitors break the service/aftermarket moat
- if order intake keeps falling after the 2027 books open

> *"när volymerna dippar så gör lastvagnarna fortfarande tvåsiffriga marginaler"*

---

### 🟢 8TRA — Traton | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Truck holding next to Volvo; margins-first Scania culture; shares pressured lately.

#### Reasoning

Same thesis as Volvo: resilient margins, strong balance sheets, and leadership from ex-Scania people with a 'margins first, volumes later' focus. The guest sees the recent 3-month weakness from China worries and soft ACT data as an opportunity rather than a thesis break.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Chinese truck competition erodes margins
- if order intake for 2027 disappoints

> *"Under tiden passar vi på att utnyttja de här möjligheterna."*

---

### 🟡 SKF-B — SKF | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Held among selected engineering companies; little specific detail given.

#### Reasoning

The guest names SKF as one of the selected engineering holdings in the fund but gives no specific thesis.

> *"Men vi har även SKF och Autoliv"*

---

### 🟢 ALIV-SDB — Autoliv | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Held; auto supplier that has gained market share, including in China.

#### Reasoning

The guest holds Autoliv despite worries about the auto sector because it has grown market share, even in China. In his words, you don't throw the baby out with the bathwater.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Autoliv loses market share in China

> *"Men de har faktiskt ökat sina marknadsandelar, även i Kina."*

---

### 🟢 ERIC-B — Ericsson | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

New position since spring: undemanding valuation, buybacks, Huawei phase-out in the EU, anti-drone optionality.

#### Reasoning

The guest re-entered after 15+ years out of the stock. He sees management now focused on shareholders, buying back its own shares at low prices instead of doing acquisitions. He does not expect rocket growth, but the valuation is undemanding. Growth pockets include the EU gradually phasing out Huawei, which eases price pressure, and defense/anti-drone technology. Its report tomorrow is the new CEO's first.

#### Sell Triggers

- if a return to value-destroying acquisitions
- if the EU Huawei phase-out stalls
- if the Q3 report shows renewed margin pressure

> *"det är inte så att vi förväntar oss någon raketartad tillväxt men å andra sidan är värderingen inte särskilt utmanande"*

---
